title: Lourinhã Formation dinosaur fauna, Portugal
summary: Around Lourinhã in west-central Portugal, Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian to Tithonian) delta and coastal-plain rocks of the Lourinhã and Alcobaça formations hold Torvosaurus, Ceratosaurus, Allosaurus, the stegosaur Dacentrurus and several sauropods. A nest of theropod eggs at Paimogo gave the only dinosaur embryos then known from Europe.

uncertainty.note: Stage bounds taken from the ICS chart (Kimmeridgian base 154.8 Ma, Tithonian top 145.0 Ma). Mateus (2006) gives only the stages; the Lourinhã Formation is mostly Tithonian and the Alcobaça Formation mainly Kimmeridgian. The id says 150 Ma, a round figure inside this range.

when.display: Late Jurassic, Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (c. 154.8 to 145.0 Ma)

where.modern_name: Lourinhã, Lisboa district, west-central Portugal (proxy pin at the town; localities lie along the coast nearby)
where.historical_name: Lourinhã and Alcobaça formations, western Iberian (Lusitanian) basin, Late Jurassic; no polities exist

importance.justification: Europe’s richest Late Jurassic dinosaur area, with genera shared with the Morrison Formation of North America.

sources.title: Late Jurassic dinosaurs from the Morrison Formation (USA), the Lourinhã and Alcobaça formations (Portugal), and the Tendaguru Beds (Tanzania): a comparison
sources.publisher: New Mexico Museum of Natural History and Science (Bulletin 36)
sources.author: Octávio Mateus

reviewer_note: Least sure of the formation boundary: the dinosaur genera are listed for the Lourinhã and Alcobaça formations together, and Allosaurus sp. in the 2003 review is from the Alcobaça beds. The pin is the town, not a single quarry. Ages are stages only.

beats.caption: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian river-delta and coastal-plain deposits, with occasional marine flooding, built up in what is now west-central Portugal.
At Paimogo near Lourinhã a nest of about one hundred theropod eggs, some with embryo bones of Lourinhanosaurus, was found in 1993.
These remained the only dinosaur embryos found in Europe by 2003, and their bone structure points to fast early growth.
